review_candidates.title: Storage Engineers (Senior/Staff) – Ceph, Linux & Enterprise Storage | Mission-Critical Infrastructure at Global Scale FinTech
review_candidates.description: The engineering challenge This is a fintech company operating business-critical infrastructure at global scale. Its storage platform must sustain high-volume, low-latency workloads while protecting the availability and integrity of internal data. This is not a conventional cloud infrastructure position. The platform runs on physical infrastructure in an on-premises, bare-metal environment. Engineers own the complete storage stack: hardware, Linux, distributed storage, automation, observability, capacity and failure recovery. If you're currently working fully on Cloud but you've done bare-metal / on-prem before and loved it we're excited to meet you! The technical challenge sits at the intersection of enterprise storage and open-source distributed systems. We therefore need an engineer who can move comfortably between Pure Storage or NetApp appliances and the internals of a production Ceph cluster. The role You will design, operate and evolve storage infrastructure supporting one of the most demanding parts of a global financial technology platform. Your work will go beyond administering storage products. You will reason about data placement, replication, quorum, failure domains, recovery behaviour, latency, throughput and capacity at scale. When the platform behaves unexpectedly, you must be able to trace the problem across disks, controllers, networks, Linux and Ceph rather than treating any part of the stack as a black box. You will become the first US-based engineer in an established international Storage team. The current team includes approximately six storage engineers and is now expanding its engineering presence in Chicago. What you’ll work on Design and operate distributed Ceph clusters across on-premises data-centre infrastructure. Manage the lifecycle and behaviour of MONs, OSDs and CRUSH maps. Engineer data placement, replication and failure-domain strategies for availability and resilience. Diagnose degraded clusters, quorum issues, failed OSDs, uneven data distribution and performance bottlenecks. Control recovery, backfilling and rebalancing without unnecessarily affecting production workloads. Investigate latency and throughput across the complete I/O path, from physical media and controllers to Linux and distributed storage services. Operate and integrate SAN, NAS, DAS and object-storage infrastructure. Work with enterprise storage technologies such as Pure Storage, NetApp, Dell EMC, IBM or Hitachi. Develop capacity models and anticipate growth before it becomes an operational constraint. Design backup, replication and disaster-recovery strategies for critical data. Automate provisioning, configuration, upgrades and recurring operational work using Python, Bash, Ansible, Puppet and Infrastructure as Code. Build actionable monitoring and alerting around cluster health, capacity, latency, saturation and failure conditions using Prometheus and Grafana. Plan and execute storage upgrades, migrations and hardware refreshes while protecting availability. Improve operational standards, documentation and incident-response procedures. What you bring Strong production experience with Ceph, not only deploying it, but operating and troubleshooting it when behaviour becomes complex. A detailed understanding of Ceph architecture, including MONs, OSDs, CRUSH, replication, quorum and recovery. Experience operating storage at meaningful scale, where capacity, performance and failure recovery require deliberate engineering. Hands-on knowledge of enterprise storage platforms such as Pure Storage, NetApp, Dell EMC, IBM or Hitachi. Experience with physical data-centre infrastructure and bare-metal environments. Deep Linux administration and troubleshooting skills. Strong knowledge of RAID, LVM, NFS, iSCSI, multipathing and file systems such as XFS, ext4 or ZFS. The ability to identify whether a problem originates in hardware, the operating system, the network or the distributed storage layer. Automation skills using Python and/or Bash. Experience with Ansible, Puppet or comparable configuration-management tooling. Experience building meaningful storage observability with Prometheus, Grafana or similar technologies. Knowledge of KVM, VMware or Infrastructure as Code is beneficial. Why this is different The storage layer is foundational to a high-volume global platform. Small design decisions can have significant consequences for latency, recovery time, capacity and system-wide availability. You will work on infrastructure where distributed-systems theory meets physical hardware and real production constraints. There is no managed cloud service abstracting away the difficult parts: the team owns the platform, understands its failure modes and engineers it for continued growth. For storage engineers who enjoy working deep in the stack, this is the kind of environment where technical judgement has visible impact.

Architectural Mindset: Ability to white-board, design, and articulate complex enterprise network and security architectures clearly. Consultative & Advisory Skills: Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate deeply technical concepts into business outcomes for both hands-on engineers and C-level executives. Commercial Mindset: Proven track record of operating in a quota-carrying or revenue-aligned environment, with a strong understanding of SaaS metrics, business value translation, and enterprise sales cycles. Security: Expertise in the security of Internet properties, including WAF, Bot Management, Firewalls, Rate Limiting, (M)TLS, Zero Trust, and SASE concepts. Performance: Expertise in the performance of Internet properties, including speed, latency, caching, video streaming, HTTP/2, and TLS 1.3.
